Rashi on Shabbat 150a:10:1.english: And their father's nakedness - Evidently, it is [considered] nakedness for a Noahide.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:11:1.english: And is speaking prohibited? But Rav Chisda said, etc. - And all of these are speech.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:11:2.hebrew: פקוח נפש - בדבר שיש בו סכנה, פקוח דיקומבימונ"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:11:2.english: Saving a life [pikuach nefesh] - In a matter in which there is danger [to life]; pikuach [means] decombremant [in Old French, clearing away an obstruction/debris].

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:11:3.english: And attending to communal needs - Such as [going] to the authorities.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:12:1.english: Theaters, circuses, and basilicas - They are types of palaces where they gathered as an assembly hall.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:12:2.hebrew: ללמדו אומנות - דהא נמי מצוה היא, דכל שאינו מלמדו אומנות מלמדו לסטות. ומצוה ילפינן מקרא בקדושין בהאשה ניקנית (ד' ל:):
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:12:2.english: To teach him a craft - For this too is a mitzvah, as whoever does not teach him a craft teaches him banditry. And [that it is] a mitzvah we derive from a verse in Kiddushin, in [the chapter] HaIshah Nikneit (30b).

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:13:1.hebrew: של מלך - של עצה שאינו שלו ואין צריך בכך, כגון הרוצה לבנות בית: "כך וכך צריך להוציא בו". ול"נ: כמו "מה לך" — מה לך ולחשבונות הללו? הרי אין צורך בהן, לא לך ולא לאחר, כגון ההיא דפרישית:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:13:1.english: Of mallakh - [Calculations] of counsel that is not his, and [that] he has no need for, such as [one who calculates regarding someone] who wants to build a house: "Such-and-such [an amount] must be spent on it." And it appears to me [that it is] like "mah lakh" ["what is it to you?"] — what have you to do with these calculations? Behold, there is no need for them, neither for you nor for another, such as that [case] which I explained.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:1:1.english: Measure - coins and gold dinars, and bring [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:2:1.hebrew: ורבו יתירה הוספת לי - לאחר שהיה ז' שנים בהמה וחזר למלכותו, היה משתבח כן. ומהו התוספת? שקשר תנין גדול — נחש גדול — בראשו של ארי, כמין אפסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:2:1.english: And surpassing greatness was added unto me - After he had been [like] a beast for seven years and returned to his kingship, he praised himself thus. And what was the addition? That he tied a large tannin — [that is,] a large serpent — to the head of a lion, like a kind of halter.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:1.english: A person may not hire workers - For it is written (Isaiah 58:13): "from pursuing your business."

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:2.hebrew: ולא יאמר לחבירו כו' - בגמרא פריך: פשיטא, כיון דהוא אסור, חבירו נמי אסור, דהא ישראל הוא, והשולחו עובר משום "לפני עור לא תתן מכשול":
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:2.english: And one may not tell his fellow, etc. - In the Gemara it asks: [Isn't this] obvious? Since he is forbidden [to do so], his fellow is also forbidden, for he is a Jew, and the one who sends him transgresses [the prohibition of], "Do not place a stumbling block before the blind."

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:3.hebrew: אין מחשיכין על התחום - לקרב עצמו בשבת עד סוף התחום ולהחשיך שם, שיהא קרוב למקום הפועלים או לפרדס להביא פירות, דכל דבר שאסור לעשותו בשבת, אסור להחשיך עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:3.english: One may not wait for nightfall at the [Shabbat] boundary - [That is,] to bring oneself close on Shabbat up to the end of the boundary and wait for nightfall there, so that he will be close to the place of the workers or to the orchard to bring produce; for anything that is forbidden to do on Shabbat, it is forbidden to wait for nightfall for its sake.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:4.hebrew: אבל מחשיך הוא - להיות קרוב לצאת לשמור פירותיו, וזה דבר המותר בשבת, לשמור פירותיו אם היו בתוך תחומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:4.english: But he may wait for nightfall - to be close [to the boundary] to go out to guard his produce; and this is a matter that is permitted on Shabbat, [namely,] to guard his produce if it were within his boundary.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:5.english: And [he] brings produce in his hand - Since his primary intention was not for this.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:6.hebrew: כלל אמר אבא שאול - נותן היה כלל בדבר זה להוסיף דברים אחרים כיוצא בו, ולקמיה מפרש לאתויי מאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:6.english: Abba Shaul stated a principle - He gave a general rule regarding this matter to include other similar things, and further on [the Gemara] explains what [it comes] to include.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:7.hebrew: כל שאני זכאי באמירתו - שאני רשאי לאומרו לחבירו או לנכרי בשבת לעשות למוצאי שבת, רשאי אני להחשיך עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:3:7.english: Anything that I am permitted to say - [Meaning] that I am permitted to say to his fellow or to a non-Jew on Shabbat to do [something] after Shabbat, I am permitted to wait for nightfall for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:4:1.hebrew: מאי שנא כו' - ופשיטא, דכיון דאמר לא ישכור, ה"ה לא יאמר לחבירו, דהא ישראל הוא כמותו ולא מצי לאוגרינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:4:1.english: What is the difference, etc. - And it is obvious, for since [the Mishnah] stated "he may not hire," the same applies [that] he may not tell another, for [that other] is a Jew like him and cannot hire them.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:4:2.hebrew: אמירה לנכרי שבות - וכבר סתמה רבי למתני', נכרי שבא לכבות, אין אומרים לו כבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:4:2.english: Telling a gentile [is a] rabbinic prohibition - And Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] already taught it anonymously in the Mishnah: "A gentile who comes to extinguish [a fire], we do not say to him, 'Extinguish [it].'"

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:5:1.hebrew: הא קמ"ל - משנה יתירה, בהדיא הוא דלא לימא ליה, אבל סתמא שרי ליה למימר:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:5:1.english: This is what it is teaching us - [The] superfluous Mishnah [teaches that it is] explicitly that he may not say [it] to him, but implicitly it is permitted for him to say [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:5:2.hebrew: הנראה - עכשיו נראה אם תעמוד עמי לערב, אם תבא אלי לכשתחשך. ושניהם יודעין שעל מנת לשוכרו לפעולתו הוא מזהירו, וכיון דלא מפרש בהדיא שרי, כדמפרש טעמא לקמן: דבור אסור, הרהור מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:5:2.english: Does it seem - Is it apparent now whether you will stand with me in the evening, [that is,] whether you will come to me when it gets dark. And both of them know that he is alerting him in order to hire him for his work, and since he does not state [it] explicitly, it is permitted, as [the Gemara] explains the reason below: speech is forbidden, [but] thought is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:7:1.english: It is permitted to think - About words of Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:7:2.hebrew: והיה מחניך קדוש - ולא כתיב ביה דבר, אלא מקום חנייתך תהא בקדושה. וטעמא משום דישראל מהרהרין תמיד בדברי תורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:7:2.english: And your camp shall be sacred - And "speech" is not written in it; rather, [it means] the place of your encampment shall be in holiness, and the reason [that contemplating Torah is forbidden there] is because Israel constantly contemplates words of Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:8:1.english: An unseemly thing [davar] - Thus, it is only prohibited to him at the time of speech [dibbur].

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:8:2.hebrew: ההיא כדרב יהודה - כלומר, לעולם "והיה מחניך קדוש" משום הרהור תורה, ואפי' אין דבור. ו"לא יראה בך ערות דבר" במילתא אחריתי מיירי, דאסור בשעת הדבור ולא בשעת הרהור, כגון להסתכל בערוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:8:2.english: That [verse] is for [the ruling of] Rav Yehuda - That is to say, in fact, "and your camp shall be holy" [is] on account of contemplation of Torah, even [when] there is no speech. And "so that He see no unseemly thing in you" refers to another matter, that is prohibited at the time of speech and not at the time of contemplation, such as gazing at nakedness.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:8:3.hebrew: עכו"ם ערום - כ"ש ישראל, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 150a:8:3.english: A naked gentile - All the more so a Jew, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Shabbat 150a:9:1.english: I might say it is fine - For he is merely like an animal.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:11:1.hebrew: ודיבור מי אסור - פי' מן התורה, דהא מדשרינן דיבור של מצוה, מכלל דמדאורייתא שרי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:11:1.english: And is speech prohibited - Meaning, by Torah law; for since we permit speech [pertaining to] a mitzvah, it follows that by Torah law it is permitted.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:11:2.hebrew: ואמר ר"א פוסקין צדקה לעניים בשבת - וא"ת: מה צריך לאתויי הא? ה"ל לאתויי מילתייהו דבית הלל [בפי"ז] (בתוספתא), דתני: "אין פוסקים צדקה אפי' להשיא יתום ויתומה, ואין משדכין על התינוקות ליארס בו, דברי בית שמאי; ובית הלל מתירין"? וצ"ל: דניחא ליה לאתויי מילתא דרבי אלעזר, דמהתם לא הוה שמעינן פסיקת צדקה לעניים, דהא לא שרי בית הלל אלא להשיא יתום ויתומה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:11:2.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: One may apportion charity for the poor on Shabbat - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] need to bring this [statement]? It should have brought the statement of Beit Hillel [in Chapter 17] (in the Tosefta), where it is taught: "One may not apportion charity, even to marry off an orphan boy or an orphan girl, and one may not negotiate matches for children to become betrothed on it [Shabbat], [these are] the words of Beit Shammai; but Beit Hillel permit [it]"? And one must say that it preferred to bring the statement of Rabbi Elazar, because from there [the Tosefta] we would not have learned [the permissibility of] apportioning charity for the poor [in general], for Beit Hillel only permitted [it] to marry off an orphan boy and an orphan girl.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:3:1.hebrew: ואין מחשיכין על התחום לשכור פועלים ולהביא פירות - השתא משמע דוקא על התחום, אבל בתוך התחום מחשיכין לשכור פועלי' ולהביא פירו'. וקשה לרבי, דבסוף פ' בכל מערבין (עירובין דף ל"ח:) תניא: "לא יהלך אדם לתוך שדהו לידע מה צריכה; כיוצא בו, לא יטייל אדם על פתח מדינה כדי שיכנס למרחץ מיד"! ואומר רבי, דהתם מינכרא מילתא דאינו מטייל אלא ליכנס למרחץ מיד אחר השבת, שעל פתח מדינה רגילים להיות מרחצאות, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דמגילה (דף ו:): "ה' מאות מעלות עשן חוץ לחומה"; אבל הכא, אין הוכחה כ"כ בתוך התחום המחשיך לשכור פועלים ולהביא פירות. וכי האי גוונא משני התם. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:3:1.english: And one may not wait for nightfall at the [Shabbat] boundary to hire workers or to bring produce - Now, this implies [that it is prohibited] specifically at the boundary, whereas within the boundary one may wait for nightfall to hire workers or to bring produce. And this is difficult for the Rabbi, for at the end of the chapter [entitled] Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 38b) it is taught [in a baraita]: "A person may not walk into his field to know what it needs; similarly, a person may not stroll at the entrance of a city in order to enter a bathhouse immediately [after Shabbat]"! And the Rabbi says that there, the matter is evident that he is only strolling in order to enter the bathhouse immediately after Shabbat, because bathhouses are commonly located at the entrance of a city, as we say in the first chapter of Megillah (6b): "Five hundred rising [columns of] smoke outside the wall"; but here, there is not so much proof [of his intention] within the boundary [for] one who waits for nightfall to hire workers or to bring produce. And in a similar manner [the Gemara] answers there. [From my teacher].

Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:4:1.hebrew: מה לי הוא ומה לי חבירו - ואם תאמר: ונימא דחבירו היינו דאמר ליה "שכור לי פועלים למחר"? וי"ל: דא"כ, מאי איריא חבירו? אפי' הוא נמי לא מצי למימר "אשכור פועלים למחר"; דעד כאן לא קאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: "מותר לאדם לומר לחבירו: לכרך פלוני אני הולך למחר", אלא משום דשאם יש בורגנין הולך, הא לאו הכי לא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:4:1.english: "What is the difference between him and his fellow?" - And if you ask: Let us say that [the case of] his fellow is where he says to him, "Hire workers for me tomorrow"? And one can answer: If so, why specifically [teach this regarding] his fellow? Even he himself also cannot say, "I will hire workers tomorrow," for Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel [that] "it is permitted for a person to say to his fellow, 'I am going to such-and-such a city tomorrow,'" only because if there are way-stations [burganin], he may go [there on Shabbat]; but if not, [it is] not [permitted].

Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:5:1.hebrew: ורבי יהושע בן קרחה היא - יש מפרש דר"ע קרוי קרחה שהיה קרח, כדתניא בפרק בתרא דבכורות (דף נח. ושם): אמר בן עזאי, כל חכמי ישראל דומין לפני כקליפת השום, חוץ מן הקרח הזה; ואומר שזה היה ר"ע, והיה לו בן ששמו יהושע, כדאמר בפרק קמא דשבועות: א"ל ר' יהושע בנו של ר"ע לר"ע. ואין נראה לר"ת, דמה שקראו בן עזאי לר"ע "קרח" בבדיחותא בעלמא, אין לנו לקרותו כן כל שעה, דלשון גנות הוא, שנא': "עלה קרח, עלה קרח" (מלכים ב ב׳:כ״ג); ואמרינן נמי לקמן (שבת דף קנב.): אמר ליה ההוא צדוקי לר' יהושע בן קרחה, מהכא לקרחינאה כמה הוי? הרי שהיה מגנה אותו על שהיה קרח. ועוד אמרי' במגילה פרק בתרא (דף כח.): שאל רבי את רבי יהושע בן קרחה, במה הארכת ימים כו'? א"ל: רבי, ברכני. א"ל: יהי רצון שתגיע לחצי ימי. ואי ר' יהושע בן קרחה בנו של ר"ע — והא קיימא לן דלא נשא ר"ע בת כלבא שבוע עד שקיבל עליו לעסוק בתורה, ואז היה בן מ', דתניא בסוף ספרי: מ' שנה שימש ת"ח, מ' שנה פירנס את ישראל, וכל ימיו ק"כ שנים; ואמרי' בקידושין פרק בתרא (דף עב.): עד שלא מת ר"ע נולד רבי. ואפילו נולד ר' יהושע בשנה ראשונה שנשאה, לא נשאר כי אם פ' שנים מר"ע; ורבי יהושע בשעה שבירך את רבי היה בן ק"מ שנים לכל הפחות, שבפחות מע' שנה לא היה מברכו, ואז היה רבי לכל הפחות בן ס', וא"כ לא היה מברכו רק מי' שנים! ועוד נראה שלא נשאה עד שעסק בי רב תרי סרי ותרי סרי שנין; נמצא כשהיה רבי יהושע בן קרחה בן ק"מ, היה רבי יותר מחצי ימיו. לכך נראה לר"ת דלא ר"ע היה, אלא איניש אחרינא היה ששמו קרחה, וקרחה הוא שם אדם כמו קרח, ונולד הרבה קודם ר' יהושע בנו של ר"ע. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:5:1.english: And it is Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa - There is one who explains that Rabbi Akiva was called "Korḥa" because he was bald [kerei'aḥ], as it was taught in a baraita in the last chapter of Bekhorot (58a and there): "Ben Azzai said: All the Sages of Israel are like a garlic peel before me, except for this bald man"; and [this commentator] says that this [bald man] was Rabbi Akiva, and he had a son whose name was Yehoshua, as it says in the first chapter of Shevuot [6a]: "Rabbi Yehoshua the son of Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Akiva." But this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for [the fact] that Ben Azzai called Rabbi Akiva "baldhead" merely in jest — we should not call him so at all times, for it is an expression of disparagement, as it is stated: "Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!" (II Kings 2:23); and we also say later (Shabbat 152a): "A certain Sadducee said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa: From here to Karḥina'ah [Baldtown], how far is it?" Thus [we see] that he was mocking him for being bald. Furthermore, we say in Megillah, the last chapter (28a): "Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa: By what [merit] have you prolonged your days, etc.? [Rabbi] said to him: My master, bless me. [Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa] said to him: May it be [God's] will that you reach half of my days." Now if Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa were the son of Rabbi Akiva — surely we hold that Rabbi Akiva did not marry the daughter of Kalba Savua until he took upon himself to engage in Torah [study], and at that time he was forty years old, as it was taught at the end of Sifre: "Forty years he served Torah scholars, forty years he sustained Israel, and all his days were one hundred and twenty years"; and we say in Kiddushin, the last chapter (72a): "Before Rabbi Akiva died, Rabbi was born." Now even if Rabbi Yehoshua was born in the first year that he married her, only eighty years remained of Rabbi Akiva['s life]; and Rabbi Yehoshua, at the time he blessed Rabbi, was at least one hundred and forty years old, for [to reach] less than seventy years he would not have blessed him, and at that time Rabbi was at least sixty years old — and if so, he would only have been blessing him with [an additional] ten years! Moreover, it appears that he did not marry her until he had studied in the house of [his] teacher for twelve and twelve [i.e., twenty-four] years; thus it turns out that when Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa was one hundred and forty, Rabbi was [already] past half of his days. Therefore it appears [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam that it was not Rabbi Akiva, but rather it was another person whose name was Korḥa — and Korḥa is a person's name, like Koraḥ — and he was born much earlier than Rabbi Yehoshua the son of Rabbi Akiva. M.R.

Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:5:2.hebrew: אומר אדם לחבירו הנראה שתעמוד עמי לערב - י"א דדווקא לחבירו, אבל לנכרי אסור, לפי שהוא [עושה] לדעת אותה [אמירה]. ואינו נראה, דהא שרינן ליה הכא משו' דדבור אסור והרהור מותר; [א"כ], ל"ש נכרי ל"ש ישראל. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 150a:5:2.english: One may say to his fellow: "Does it seem that you will join me this evening?" - Some say that [this is permitted] specifically to his fellow [Jew], but to a gentile it is forbidden, because he acts according to that statement. But this does not seem [correct], for we permit it here because [explicit] speech is forbidden whereas thought is permitted; if so, there is no difference between a gentile and a Jew. [From my teacher].
